blocks.text: The creator of controversial AI actor Tilly Norwood has teased her next project with Lion King co-director Rob Minkoff .

The audience at today’s British Screen Forum in London were treated to a clip of Storm Dogs , as Eline Van der Velden took them behind the scenes of the making of the AI-assisted movie, first revealed by Deadline a few weeks back.

links.text: first revealed by Deadline a few weeks back.

blocks.text: Van der Velden, who runs the film’s production company Particle6, said the movie mixes real actors with some AI. Having AI actors play toddlers and dogs made life easier on set, she joked.

blocks.text: She also said her team had built a tech platform made “by creatives for creatives” to help produce the film.
Watch on Deadline
“It’s really hard to do AI well, that’s why there is so much slop,” said Van der Velden. “AI might reduce your budget by 50% but it won’t go to 0%. That’s why you’ve not seen a good AI feature yet.”
She is confident Storm Dogs, which counts Minkoff at the helm, can buck the trend.
Van der Velden said her team is “pushing to get real actors back on screen even in this new medium,” while Particle6 has given jobs to 30 budding filmmakers in the past year.

“I believe the industry will grow as a result of this technology,” she added. “Brands will want to come in, looking to be the next Mattel. It’s not dissimilar from the 1920s when the talkies came in.”
Tilly “succeeded in sparking a debate”
Van der Velden reflecting on a year in which her controversial AI creation Norwood has dominated chatter around AI and the industry.
Norwood “succeeded in sparking a debate” about rules and regulation around industry AI, she said.
“She really cut through the noise,” added Van der Velden. “She embodied the fear we’re all feeling when it comes to AI.”
Van der Velden, who is an actor herself, said Norwood was an “interesting experiment to see how my skills as an actor would translate in this new medium.”
“Tilly is me, I am Tilly,” she added.
Van der Velden was speaking at the British Screen Forum after former Amazon UK boss Chris Bird, who now runs AI venture Hawkshead .
Bird said AI is allowing practices developed by the streaming giants to be “replicated for the independent industry,” which can lead to “better creative decisions.”
